Cyber Attack Disrupts South African Automotive Firms, Metair Investments Ltd Impacted

A major cyber attack targeting the South African automotive industry is currently disrupting operations at several major firms, including Metair Investments Ltd. The incident, which began on Thursday morning, involves a sophisticated ransomware assault on companies' IT systems, halting production lines and delaying shipments.

Metair Investments Ltd confirmed in a statement that its Johannesburg-based facilities experienced a "significant system outage" due to unauthorized access to its networks. The company said it has engaged cybersecurity experts and is working with law enforcement to contain the breach, but warned that “production schedules and parts distribution have been materially affected.”

Industry sources estimate that at least four large automotive manufacturers and parts suppliers have been hit, with supply chain delays expected to cascade across the sector. “We are seeing widespread disruption, particularly in electronic parts tracking and logistics management,” said Thabo Mokoena, spokesperson for the National Automotive Association of South Africa. “Production has slowed or stopped at several sites, and there is concern about meeting export commitments.”

As of Friday afternoon, ransom demands had reportedly been issued to some firms, but it is unclear whether any payments have been made. Analysts say the attack comes at a sensitive time for local automakers, who are already grappling with global supply chain pressures. “This cyber attack exposes critical vulnerabilities in the industry’s digital infrastructure,” said Nomsa Dlamini, an independent cybersecurity consultant. “Recovery could take days or even weeks, and the financial impact may be significant.”

Unions representing automotive workers have called for urgent action to secure employee data and restore operations. Companies, including Metair Investments Ltd, have yet to provide a timeline for full system restoration as investigations continue.
